facets.rationale: The bounded subject is Plan's non-mutating conversion of admitted design intent into a governed, evidence-bearing executable planning model, not execution itself.

The model independently retains Implementation Layering and its four layers, Work Pack, delivery slices, shared context, waves, tasks, implementation-detail specs, SWUs, validation and gap state, execution choreography, and execution-entry contracts.

The artifact materializes containment and ordering from Work Pack through waves, tasks, and SWUs; layer ordering and promotion; task and SWU dependencies; slice mapping; route/frontier coverage; and closeout succession.
Plan artifact evidence, Work Pack current state, proof-only implementation-readiness evidence, later exact acceptance, and runtime admission are distinct states with separate claim ceilings.

Activation, complexity, task detail, SWU atomicity, first-unit narrowness, recomposition, validation coverage, blocker/gap ownership, closeout completeness, route coverage, readiness preflight, and protected-effect stops remain independently testable.

Plan prepares a selected one-SWU handoff, finite frontier, exact routes, typed unit validation, context-builder-ready anchors, closeout continuity, and bounded prerequisite return without performing the work.

Plan owns planning artifacts and execution contracts but cannot alter upstream design, execute SWUs, accept the final candidate, grant mutation admission, promote authority, publish, release, or deploy.

includes: Canonical executable plan and coordinator control panel
Objective, delivery slices, task and SWU manifests, validation strategy, blockers, gate status, output mode, active layer window, links, and current execution state
excludes: Layer philosophy owned by Implementation Layering
Deep task-local detail when useful split task files exist
Execution of any task or SWU
The retired Implementation Plan as a second executable source of truth

Disagreement with wave or task artifacts keeps its gate blocked until reconciled

includes: One global decision-first governance lens over the plan
L0-L3 decision boundaries, minimum working units, included and deferred scope, exit evidence, and promotion decisions
conditions: Every plan has exactly one global Implementation Layering artifact
Work Pack waves, tasks, and SWUs map back to its decisions
Later layers preserve guarantees established by earlier layers

conditions: Its exit evidence supports continue, pivot, or stop
Its deferred scope remains explicit

includes: The repeatable working slice that tests whether repeatability or hardening is credible

includes: The policy, governance, reliability, validation, and degraded-mode proof
excludes: Scale or packaging concerns explicitly deferred to L3
conditions: Promotion from L1 cites prior-layer evidence
Its exit decision is scale, remediate, or stop

Its exit decision is pilot, package, or defer

includes: One outcome-bearing partition of the delivery boundary with layer, dependencies, and validation
excludes: A task with no outcome or validation
conditions: Each slice produces one or more tasks

includes: Source contracts, traceability, cross-task decisions and gaps, and global assumptions shared by multiple tasks

includes: One task objective with layer and slice mapping, source contracts, dependencies, blockers or gaps, SWUs, synchronization rules, and completion evidence

A split task file is a useful executable contract

conditions: Required for every medium or high complexity execution task
Missing acceptance-critical detail blocks or routes to an explicit decision

includes: The smallest executable implementation step below a task and above source edits
One parent task, one primary behavior or decision, dependencies, explicit write scope, source context, done criteria, acceptance evidence, validation, execution owner, and handoff note
excludes: Several independently verifiable behaviors bundled for convenience
A source edit with no independently reviewable acceptance boundary
A whole multi-SWU task handed off without selection
conditions: Each SWU belongs to exactly one task
Medium and high complexity non-exempt tasks decompose into SWUs
Closure-only exemptions are limited to the declared verification categories

includes: Execution ordering with a wave goal, layer mapping, entry gate, included tasks or SWUs, dependency order, parallelization boundary, and exit evidence

includes: Cross-task choreography, waves, stage coverage, closure obligations, and parallelization boundaries for medium and high complexity work

includes: The declared dependency and write-scope conditions under which tasks or SWUs may execute concurrently

Cross-team ownership, irreversible migration risk, or multiple unresolved gate dependencies raise high-complexity concern

includes: An unresolved condition affecting acceptance criteria or a mandatory gate

conditions: It names impact, owner, and resolution route

excludes: An acceptance-critical unresolved blocker mislabeled as a flag

excludes: Baseline work bundled with later responsive, projection, interaction, or regional work

includes: Evidence that the selected coherent unit and the remaining plan recompose into the approved design and delivery boundary
excludes: Path or count equality treated as semantic coverage
A unit that achieves an unrelated local outcome
conditions: Failed recomposition blocks mutation-capable routing

includes: Independent assessment of smallest coherent unit, SWU atomicity and split analysis, first-unit narrowness, recomposition, hidden acceptance-critical gaps, deferred complexity, implementation detail, and navigation

conditions: Any acceptance-critical blocker keeps the gate blocked

includes: The complete ordered set of unfinished execution units captured by the Work Pack
